title: You didn’t fall by accident.
paragraphs:
You didn’t fall by accident.
You were led… or lured.
That’s the difference.

A TEST is from God.
A TEMPTATION is not.
But they can look the same on the outside.

A test is meant to prove you.
A temptation is meant to pull you down.

Same pressure.
Different purpose.
Look at James 1:13–14:
“God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone; but each one is tempted when he is drawn away by his own desires…”

God tests your faith.
Your flesh feeds your temptation.

A test says:
“Trust Me even when it’s hard.”

A temptation whispers:
“Take it now, even if it’s wrong.”
Think of Genesis 22.
God tested Abraham.

It wasn’t to destroy him.
It was to reveal his obedience… and deepen his trust.
Now look at Genesis 3.
The serpent tempted Eve.

Not to strengthen her—
but to separate her from God.

Same tree.
Same moment.
Different voices.
And here’s the part we miss…

A test can become a temptation
when we stop trusting God in the middle of it.

That’s where many fall.
Not at the beginning—
but in the waiting.
But Jesus…
Oh, Jesus.
In Matthew 4, He was both tested and tempted in the wilderness.

Hungry.
Alone.
Pressed.
The enemy said, “Turn stones to bread.”
Temptation.
But Jesus answered with Scripture.
Victory.
Here’s your anchor:

Tests build you.
Temptations bait you.

One leads to maturity.
The other leads to sin—if you bite.
But hear this clearly—
You are not helpless.
Through Christ, you are not a slave to temptation.

There is always a way out.
Always.

If you’re in a test right now—hold on.
If you’re in temptation—run to Jesus, not from Him.

Grace is not waiting after you win.
Grace meets you in the fight.

From pressure to purpose.
From craving to calling.
From test… to testimony.
